proposals.before: In Shaotai year 2 (550), as a southern-river strongman he was made roaming-cavalry general by precedent.
proposals.after: In Shaotai year 2 (556), as a southern-river strongman he was made roaming-cavalry general by precedent.
proposals.reason: Shaotai 2 of Liang Jingdi is AD 556, not 550; the parenthetical Western year is wrong.

proposals.before: In Shaotai year 2, as a southern-river magnate Tanlang was by precedent made roaming-cavalry general.
proposals.after: In Shaotai year 2 (556), as a southern-river magnate Tanlang was by precedent made roaming-cavalry general.
proposals.reason: Add correct Western year for Shaotai 2 (AD 556) for consistency with chronology.

proposals.before: In Shaotai year 2 (550) he was made interior administrator of Linchuan.
proposals.after: In Shaotai year 2 (556) he was made interior administrator of Linchuan.

proposals.before: Collation variant: (Tianjia). In spring of the third year, [3] Emperor Wen pardoned southern-river people led astray by Di and ordered Jiang inspector Wu Mingche to command all forces with Gao inspector Huang Fading and Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu against Di.
proposals.after: In spring of Tianjia year 3 (562), [3] Emperor Wen pardoned southern-river people led astray by Di and ordered Jiang inspector Wu Mingche to command all forces with Gao inspector Huang Fading and Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu against Di.
proposals.reason: Editorial collation gloss was left in the idiomatic English; render as a normal dated sentence with Western year.

proposals.before: At Poyang, Xinwu cave lord Yu Xiaoqing rose for Lin.
proposals.after: At Pencheng, Xinwu cave lord Yu Xiaoqing rose for Lin.
proposals.reason: 湓城 is Pencheng (Jiujiang), not Poyang; same error recurs for 湓城 elsewhere in the chapter.

proposals.before: We now send pacifying-the-south equal-in-honor's army marshal, Xiangdong duke's chancellor Liu Guangde, with pacifying-the-west marshal Sun Xiao, North Xin'ai administrator Lu Guangda, credential-bearing pacifying-the-south general and Wu inspector Marquis of Pengze Lu Xida, and ten thousand armored men, marching from Xingkou.
proposals.after: We now send the Zhen-nan equal-to-the-three-dukes' army marshal and chancellor to the Duke of Xiangdong, Liu Guangde; concurrent Pingxi marshal Sun Xiao; administrator of Northern Xincai Lu Guangda; and credential-bearing Annan general, Wu inspector, Marquis of Pengze Lu Xida, with ten thousand armored men, marching out from Xingkou.
proposals.reason: 北新蔡 is Northern Xincai, not Xin'ai; office string is awkwardly fused.

proposals.before: Baoying armed Di with troops and stores; Liu Yi also sent his second son, the Loyal Subject, to follow.
proposals.after: Baoying armed Di with troops and stores; Liu Yi also sent his second son Zhongchen to follow.
proposals.reason: 忠臣 is the son's personal name Zhongchen, not a title 'the Loyal Subject'.

proposals.before: Next spring Andu smashed the palisades. Yi and his second son Chuxin fled to Chen Baoying. Several thousand followers, men and women, were taken.
proposals.after: Next spring Andu smashed the palisades. Yi and his second son Zhongchen fled to Chen Baoying. Several thousand followers, men and women, were taken.
proposals.reason: 第二子忠臣 is Zhongchen, not Chuxin.

proposals.before: In Shaotai year 2, for aiding the court, he was made bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, trust-military general, inspector of Jingzhou with concurrent Dongyang prefect, and marquis of Yongxing county [7] with a fief of five hundred households. On [7]: the Southern History reads Yongjia.
proposals.after: In Shaotai year 2 (556), for aiding the court, he was made bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, trust-military general, inspector of Jinzhou with concurrent Dongyang prefect, and marquis of Yongxing county [7] with a fief of five hundred households. On [7]: the Southern History reads Yongjia.
proposals.reason: 縉州 is Jinzhou, not Jingzhou; add Western year 556.

proposals.before: Collation variant: still; adopted reading: but also be promoted and rewarded.
proposals.after: but also be promoted and rewarded.
proposals.reason: Remove collation meta-prose from idiomatic English.

decisions.reason: Shaotai year 2 was AD 556; the parenthetical 550 is six years too early.
Adding the correct Western equivalent makes the literal field consistent with the dated idiomatic field.
This second occurrence of Shaotai year 2 likewise corresponds to AD 556, not 550.

decisions.after: In spring of Tianjia year 3 (562), Emperor Wen pardoned the southern-river people who had been misled by Di and ordered Jiangzhou inspector Wu Mingche to command all forces, together with Gaozhou inspector Huang Fading and Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu, in a campaign against Di.
decisions.reason: The English should translate the historical sentence directly, supply the correct date, and omit collation apparatus and bracket markers from the prose.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 天嘉三年春，世祖乃下詔

decisions.after: When Wang Lin reached Pencheng, Yu Xiaoqing, lord of the Xinwu cave settlement, raised troops in support of him.
decisions.reason: 湓城 is Pencheng near Jiujiang, distinct from Poyang (鄱陽), which appears elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.after: We now dispatch Liu Guangde, army marshal to the general who guards the south and chancellor to the Duke of Xiangdong; Sun Xiao, concurrently army marshal to the general who pacifies the west; Lu Guangda, administrator of northern Xincai; and Lu Xida, bearer of credentials, general who pacifies the south, inspector of Wuzhou, and Marquis of Pengze, with ten thousand armored men marching from Xingkou.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly restores Northern Xincai but leaves the office string cramped. This revision separates each appointee and office without dropping any title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 北新蔡太守魯廣達，持節、安南將軍

decisions.reason: 忠臣 is the son's personal name Zhongchen, not the common noun phrase 'the Loyal Subject.'
The same son is named Zhongchen here; Chuxin has no basis in the characters 忠臣.

decisions.after: In Shaotai year 2 (556), for aiding the court, he was made bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, general who inspires martial might, inspector of Jinzhou, and concurrently administrator of Dongyang; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing County with five hundred households.
decisions.reason: 縉州 is Jinzhou, the date is AD 556, and the collation marker and Southern History note do not belong inside the translated prose.

decisions.after: He was also rewarded and promoted.
decisions.reason: 仍加賞擢 is ordinary narrative prose. The current output exposes collation machinery, while the proposal begins with an ungrammatical lowercase conjunction.

claimRetractions.reason: The Loyal Subject is not an alias; it was created by translating Zhongchen's personal name as a common noun phrase.
